<reason>CON won the live policy-design fight. After pressure, CON made the debate easier to decide by showing PRO’s Safari/Firefox proof supported narrower tracking prevention, not the motion’s maximal ad-and-tracker floor, and that Chrome’s gap is more naturally an antitrust problem than a statutory architecture for every OS. PRO’s coverage-gap and “choose the switch” framing stayed vivid, but left funding, “robust” definition, and liability under-repaired. CON’s clipped opening was a real cost, not enough to erase the clearer comparative case.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON’s R2 answer that Safari/Firefox shipped narrow tracking prevention, not ad blocking, and survived via calibrated/ad-funded deals—defusing PRO’s strongest pressure question and exposing the leap to a crude everywhere-mandate.</best_rebuttal>
